title: A window from a process that outlives a workspace's sleep can land in the sleeping workspace
body:
Sleeping a workspace (`State::sleep_workspace` in `decade/src/server/compositor.rs`) kills the programs decade started in it and asks its other windows to close. A process that survives, such as a program a shell in the workspace started outside decade, can still open a window afterwards. `Tab::place` no longer matches panes of a sleeping workspace by app id, but `launched_from` and the fallback to the workspace on screen can still put the window in the sleeping workspace. The window then sits in a workspace that says it is asleep.

A pending pane screenshot (`capturing` or `asking`) for a workspace that goes to sleep also ends with whatever the empty pane yields.

## Open

- Whether such a window should wake the workspace, go to the workspace on screen, or be closed.
close_reason: Landed in b9df6e8. A window placed in a sleeping workspace goes to the workspace on screen, which wakes if asleep. Pending screenshots (capturing or asking) answer with a went-to-sleep error when the workspace sleeps.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/5da9dd6b
notes.text: Jack chose the workspace on screen. When placement picks a sleeping workspace, the window goes to the workspace on screen. If that one is asleep too, it wakes, since Jack is looking at it. A pane screenshot still pending when its workspace sleeps answers with an error saying the workspace went to sleep.
